Position Title: Clinical Nurse Specialist (Grade 2), Custodial Mental Health, MRRC Centre, TFT up to 2 May 2027

If you are passionate about delivering healthcare with the greatest impact, then come and join us at the Justice Health and Forensic Mental Health Network (JHFMHN). We are Just the Placeto grow your career and be part of a valued team delivering care where it's needed most!

Be part of a supportive environment, where you can apply your skills to address complex healthcare needs while broadening your treatment capabilities to maximise patient outcomes. 

We are a challenging yet rewarding place to take your career even further. With industry-leading safety standards, you can focus on doing your best work alongside skilled colleagues while gaining job training to progress your career.

The Role

The Clinical Nurse Specialist 2 (CNS2) mental health providesa high standard of care in the assessment & management of mental health issues as well as discharge planning and transfer of care. 

The successful applicant must demonstrate strong clinical leadership in the ongoing development & review of treatment planning and clinical review systems for patients with mental health concerns.

This position requires the ability to manage multiple tasks simultaneously. The position holder will be required to process and manage complex and simultaneous issues as part of their regular workload and must demonstrate the ability to enhance organisational performance through collaboration and development of good working relationships with Corrective Services-NSW and JH&FMHN more broadly to provide a "whole of service" approach to patient care.

ESSENTIAL REQUIREMENTS

Current authority to practice as a Registered Nurse with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia and a current NSW driver's licence. 

Three years full-time experience working in mental health and post-graduate qualification in mental health.

Our Service and Team

Custodial Mental Health (CMH) is a specialist mental health service within the Justice Health and Forensic Mental Health Network that provides a range of mental health services to adults in NSW correctional centres.

CMH includes a specialist mental health team with mental health nurses (MHNs), nurse practitioners (NPs), Aboriginal Mental Health Clinicians, psychiatrists, career medical officers (CMOs), and psychiatry registrars who are supported by administrative and managerial staff.

CMH clinicians work alongside staff from other clinical streams and CSNSW staff, including Psychology, Offender Services and Programs, and Custodial Operations staff in the provision of mental health services. Mental health services begin at the point of reception and continue through to release from custody or transfer to another correctional centre.

Your salary plus superannuation is just the beginning. You'll have access to:

. Additional allowances that may apply.

. Access to salary packaging benefits.

. A fitness passport (if you're eligible) 

. Free on-site parking to minimise your commute time.

. Fantastic training & education opportunities available.

Diversity and Inclusivity

We are an equal-opportunity employer. We employ all ages and genders, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, culturally and linguistically diverse groups, the LGBTQIA+ community, veterans, refugees and people with disability.

*This is also a Targeted Aboriginal Position. Preference will be given to applicants of Aboriginal descent. Exemption is claimed under Section 21 of the Anti-Discrimination Act 1977

 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 

 

READY TO APPLY?

The first step is to submit your resume and answers to the following targeted questions:

Describe a time when you were presented with challenging behaviour. What strategies did you use to de-escalate the situation.

Provide an example demonstrating your negotiation and influencing skills to leverage resources from multi-functional work teams to deliver successful patient outcomes. What were your keys to success?

Describe a time when you had to manage multiple tasks in your clinical practice, and what methods you used in order to prioritise your clinical activities.

The Role

The primary purpose of the Assistant in Nursing (AIN) at the Forensic Hospital is to provide support in the delivery of high-quality mental health care to patients under the supervision of a Registered Nurse (RN). The role is limited to delegated activities appropriate to their level of knowledge and skill and is commensurate with their education and experience.

The Forensic Hospital is a high-secure forensic mental health facility in New South Wales, operated by Justice Health NSW. This facility provides specialist, therapeutic inpatient care for adults and adolescent forensic, correctional and high-risk civil patients. 

A multidisciplinary team of medical, nursing and allied health professionals are dedicated to providing a care across the clinical spectrum, from high dependency and acute care, to long stay and rehabilitation care.

Midwife

Eligibility Open to Everyone

Midwifery Group Practice
Take your midwifery career further while delivering true continuity of care.

WHERE YOU'LL BE AND WHAT YOU'LL DO

YNLHN offers an all-risk Midwifery Group Practice, enabling midwives to work autonomously within a continuity of care caseload model. Our MGP model is recognised for its high levels of professional satisfaction and strong clinical support, allowing you to work to the full scope of your midwifery practice while delivering truly woman-centred care. Our Midwifery Group Practice offers you support and flexibility while meeting your work life balance.

About the Role

As an MGP Midwife, you will provide continuity of care across the entire maternity journey, including:

Antenatal care and clinics from 12-14 weeks

Intrapartum care

Postnatal care in hospital and at home

Collaborative multidisciplinary clinics

Lactation support

Childbirth and parenting education

This role supports autonomous practice while working within a collaborative, progressive, and supportive multidisciplinary environment.

Our MGP Services
Across five MGP sites, YNLHN supports approximately 600 women and families each year:

Our Locations

Clare - the heart of South Australia's renowned Clare Valley, offering a relaxed lifestyle surrounded by world-class wineries, scenic landscapes, and a strong sense of community

Crystal Brook - A thriving agricultural hub and gateway to the Flinders Ranges, located 200 km north of Adelaide. Close to Bowman Park and the iconic Heysen Trail.

Jamestown - A historic town nestled along Belalie Creek, near the Southern Flinders Ranges and Bundaleer Forest, Australia's oldest plantation forest.

Port Pirie - A vibrant regional city on the Spencer Gulf, close to the Flinders Ranges, offering caf s, markets, arts, and strong community connections.

Wallaroo - A popular coastal town just 160 km north of Adelaide, famous for its beaches, fishing, diving, and award-winning tourism appeal.

What We're Looking For

To be successful in this role, you will demonstrate:

Recent midwifery practice across the full maternity continuum

Strong clinical knowledge within woman-centred continuity models

Well-developed communication, leadership, and clinical escalation skills

Experience in quality improvement and risk management

Digital capability to support safe, effective patient care

About Us - Yorke & Northern Local Health Network

YNLHN delivers quality, accessible healthcare to communities ranging from major regional centres to remote rural towns.

Our vision: To be a global leader in rural and remote healthcare.
Our values: Community, Compassion, Quality, Integrity, Equity, and Curiosity - guiding how we care, collaborate, and lead.

WHO ARE WE AND WHAT WE OFFER?

The Yorke and Northern Local Health Network (YNLHN) supports and fosters a culture in which employees feel they belong and feel safe in their work environment encouraging all people to use their talents and be valued and rewarded for their contributions.

A career in the YNLHN can be very rewarding and comes with great lifestyles benefits. Not to mention your choice of scenery from farm to ocean, vineyards, and the Southern Flinders Ranges.

AT YNLHN we offer opportunities to extend, progress or consolidate your career with us in the following ways:

Salary package a range of benefits (including living expenses such as mortgage, rent, utility bills and groceries) and meal entertainment expenses Click here more information.

Access to professional development opportunities, enabling staff to build skills across a diverse range of services while contributing to high-quality, person-centred care for the community.

Support for you and your family via our free Employee Assistance Program.

35% on call allowance

WHAT ELSE DO YOU NEED TO KNOW-WHAT IS ESSENTIAL FOR SUCCESS?

Working in this environment, it is important to us that we employ people with the utmost integrity and commitment to providing a service to the highest possible standard to all visitors. To ensure that we meet that commitment there are a few checks that you will be required to undertake. These are detailed on the Role Description, but are likely to include:

Registration or eligibility for enrolment as a Nurse with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia and hold, or be eligible to hold, a current practicing certificate.

Undergo employment screening and meet immunisation requirements.

Please contact us, if you have any queries. Further information please see: Addressing vaccine preventable disease: Occupational assessment, screening and vaccination policy and in the application to help guide you.

NEED TO RELOCATE?

Relocation financial support may be negotiated, subject to eligibility. See what is available here: Relocation support | SA Health. 

OUR COMMITMENT TO DIVERSITY & INCLUSION

At YNLHN we pride ourselves on being an Equal Opportunity employer committed to providing an inclusive workplace that embraces diversity and inclusion for all employees. We encourage applications from people of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander descent, culturally diverse backgrounds, disability, all genders, and LGBTQIA+SB community and people who live with disability and-or neurodivergence.
